Sanskrit_OCR_Text: रु २ तेश्रविष्ठादौ सूर्याचन्द्रमसाबुदकः सार्पाधे दक्षिणाऽर्कस्तूमाघः श्रावणे रा १ योः सदा॥ई॥धर्मरद्धिरपांप्रस्थः क्षपौ सउदगन्तौ। दक्षिणेतो विपर्य स्तो षएमुहृत्ययनेनतु॥७॥द्विगुणं सप्तमं वाऽनुरुयनाद्यंत्रयोदश॥चतु र्थंदंश मंचैव द्विगुर्माद्यंबऊले ष्यतो॥८॥वसुस्त्वष्टा भ गोजश्च मि त्रसर्पाश्विनोजलं। धाताक श्राद्यायना श्राऊं पंचैनभ खस्तुना ॥ भांशास्युरषकाः कार्याः पक्षा द्वादश चो हताः॥एकादशगुणास्योनः भु क्लैर्दै चै इवायदि॥१०॥१२॥कार्याभांशाष्टकास्थानि कलायेकान् विंशतिः॥

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: श्रीगणेशायनमः श्रीमद्गुरुस्पोनमः॥ यदेतत्सदपंचमंगणपतेर्यद्दीद्यरत्त्वांबु डंगेंडस्छअमरारणीमधुधियानातिस्पृशंतिष्ठुः॥ मेंझारब्धनिदत्ताचिन्तजमहालक्ष्मो दियकिंचित्यदान्मंजुसज्जातिशांतिंतबिदधतीसत्तांडयेकालिकां॥१परंयरेतरङ्गणा हियुक्तनविष्श्वरोमोदिबिंचंयुतः॥अंगारपाब्हंविजहायूनमौकरोरिपछीतरंगो शियैबः॥२कुर्येरमलशास्त्रस्पवैचित्र्यंमुमनोहरं॥रामोदेवबिदोऽजिरेत्योपुरोत्लंब्य नेर्युथा॥३प्रादावजीएकुजदेवगंगामम्पद्याधिधिइमपिदैवयिंदावरिष्ठं॥स म्पकलूंडोस्वस्तुरवकूएविणिर्रयार्थंपैराइयंरमजशास्त्रविद्नृपच्छेवण॥रंध्रेयज्ञ मितोबिंदुः समरंध्रछयंडुतः॥वाममार्गेणविज्ञेयंक्रमास्थानचलक्ष्यै॥परिरेवेकां जायतेरेखावृत्तेफांजायतेतथा॥रेखाशास्त्र्स्यमायोगाज्ञायतेरूप्मेयचा५चतु स्थानाइहंक्रमपदनाथपंचमंक्रिदं ततः षष्ठंयोक्तंतदुपरिमंदचाएममितं॥द्द्योर्यो गेयोगेनवमदशमेज्ञानव्ययगे क्रमारज्ञेयंस्पष्टंतरतुनवमाद्योगजभिते॥१७विष्श्व गैदेवैरसंज्ञेशचशकलचहुरोदिते॥तयोर्येगेप्वदशंतदा द्द्योगजृपं॥ प्रथ शकलक्रमः॥ लस्यानेकुदाखिले ततोकऊदरवारिजं॥उमातफरहोचैवो

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: कलाप्य्किशंकं तथा॥९॥ कुमराश्चषयानश्व तथा नक्षत्तारवारिजः॥ ततो नक्षत्रस्तै स्थिताश्च तथैव वारिजे तथा॥१०॥ नक्षत्रातावदारिखे जडमे तरेत्वाक्रमात्॥ षड्-चंद्रशंकनानां च क्रमो यं परिकीर्तितः॥११॥ मध्यरेखापरिज्ञानमाह॥१३॥ द्वै वेदग्नमधोद्विज त्रयस्पार्धै धनं ध्यानं विषतिरगेन चांध्रकिशं॥ वेदैकरायतितथोर्ध्दीगा वरे खातस्याधोगगनमध्ये पुनस्तथैव ॥१२॥ प्रैर्लै चकब्दारवी जंबु स्टांक बुद्दर्वारिजं॥ तद्देयगदितं स्पष्टं शकज्जरमजेषु च ॥१३॥ रेवाणां ना यति च त्रुटयः क्रमेण प्रचितं द्ययनध्र रे जैमान संज्ञं॥ व्यस्तांत ह्यादि तरी खाये चातोग्द्द् श्न्ने ध्दृं जकमथो ततश्रशून्यं ॥१४॥ फरहस्यिपरि री तगानकी स्या द्घादि रे रेखचतुमध्वगेप्पद्धी॥ गगने वक्र तासिधंतदास्याद्विपरीतेजतामा रये लागी ज्या ॥१५॥ अथ धोरेव्याहर्द्ध तदुपरिनन्नो उपरिगतोषुज जो लो ना ये हुर्रमसवरे श्चापि कुमरा ॥ नाये ह्यस्ता सास्पा छज्ञ विधि विंशे शंभुन ने शया ज्ञा रखो ज्ञे यो विमलतर म जे शाक जगते ॥१६॥ शून्यवादयस्पार्घादि योर्द्ध स्वारिष्टि तंततस्तुरै खाश्थ यके क्रमेण॥ तथा च शून्य त्रयमह्र शंखि तं रे रेख दास्या त्तदध्वश्रतियगा॥१७॥ नक्षत्रतारवारिज संज्ञ के नाये चादंतव रवारिजसं ज्ञ कं ते तथा न्यतः॥ व्यस्तांत भवति यदा रिवला निधं स द्विजेयंस काभमिदं
Final_Translation: Like the *kalāpi-kiśaṅka*, and similarly the *kumāra*, *chaṣayāna*, and the *nakṣatra-tāravārija*. Then the *nakṣatras*, situated in that manner, and likewise in the *vārija*. Fractions of the lines do not exist; [thus] accumulated in sequence, the *dvayana-dhra-re-jaiman* designation [arises]. Reversed at the end, from the beginning, towards the other line, and below [it is]... then zero. Beginning with zero, half, etc., up to half, situated in the *vārija*, then four lines respectively in that order. And thus, three zeros, marked... give the line, and below it...   That which is designated as *nakṣatra-tāravārija*, and at the end, that designated as *tāravārija*, and others similarly. When it is reversed at the end, knowing the strength of the enemy, this should be understood by the twice-born as being like this.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: श्रीगणेशायनमः॥ श्रीमधुरूपोनमः॥ यदेतत्पदपंकजं गणापतेर्यद्दीधरत्क्वांबु जंगंडस्थलमद्यरायणि मधुधिया नातिस्पृशंतिमुहुः॥ मेजीरहू निदत्ताचित्तज महातेजो दियकिं चित्यदानमंजुलमतीशद्दि तंबिदधती सत्पांडयेकालिनां॥१॥ परं वरं तङ्गणा दियुक्तंनविद्वयेग्यो दिविचंद्रयुक्तलः॥ अगारनाहंविजहाय नू मौक्षरो तिप्ष्ठं तरगो श्रियैः॥२॥ कुर्य्यरमलशास्त्र स्पवैचित्रपंस्तुमनोहरं॥ रामोदेवविदोंज्ञितै पुरोहंलयव नेर्युथा॥३॥ प्रादावजीष्टकुसददेवगणंगणम्पश्चाधिधिङमपिदैवविदोंवारिษं॥स म्पक्यलडो स्थसुरवक्कयविनिरैया थंपैशह्यंरमजशास्त्रविदं नुप्ष्ट्येव्ण॥रंध्रेत्रज मितोबिंदुः समरं ध्ययंहूडः॥वाममार्गेणाविज्ञेयं क्रमाश्र्चानयछष्ठ्यै॥परेरेवेकां जायतरेवा शून्येपांजावते तथा॥ रेखाश्र्चन्यणमायोगेज्ञायते शून्येमयं चाऽचतु स्थानानांर्हू क्रमपदनायं पंचमञ्चिदं ततः॥ षष्ठंयोक्तं तदुपरिमंदंचाणमितं॥ द्वयोयो गेयोगेनवमदशमेज्ञानव्ययगे क्रमारतारेयंस्पृष्टंतरतु नवमाद्योगज निते॥१९॥ विश्वे पदेवैर्लसे चशुकलेचतुरोदिते॥ तयोर्येगे परं वदशंतदा द्वयोर्गजं नृपं॥ प्रध शकलंक्रमः॥ लस्त्या नः कूडदारिलं ततोकूडारवारिजं॥ उमातफरहो चैवो
Final_Translation: Salutation to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Salutation to Śrī Madhurūpa.   That which is the lotus-foot of Gaṇapati, which the intoxicated bee—having settled upon the temple of the elephant king—does not cease to touch repeatedly with the desire for honey; may that grant auspicious brilliance, adorning the assembly of the noble Pāṇḍyas, possessing supreme majesty, arising from the mind, charming, and showering every desired boon.  Better by far is that associated with Gaṇa, not known to the ignorant, just as the moon in the sky is attended by stars. I have not abandoned my home, standing firmly for the sake of the supreme imperishable glory.   May he, Rāmadevavid, make the manifold nature of the science of dance most charming, as performed by the Yavanas according to the wise.  Having first propitiated the gathering of gods, and then bowing to Gaṇapati, and also honoring the assembly of astrologers, [the author] now clearly sets forth the science of dance and music for the delight of the wise.  The bindu placed in the aperture is known as *samāndhya*; the *hūḍa* is to be understood through the left path; and the sequential order belongs to the sixth.   When one or two arise on the other side, and similarly zeros are manifested in the place [of digits], by the combination of lines and zeros, zero is known as the fourth.   Of the places, this is the fifth, designated in order as the *hūḍa* pada. Thereafter, the sixth is stated, and above that is the *maṇca* measure. By the combination of the two, the ninth and tenth are known respectively, pertaining to expenditure of knowledge, arising from the conjunction of the ninth [and other factors].  Shining with all the gods, in the bright fortnight when four [tithis] have arisen, upon the combination of those two, he declares the supreme [truth] then, producing an elephant and a king from the union of the two.   Such is the sequence of the first part: the *lastya*, then the *kūḍadārila*, then the *kūḍāravārija*, and likewise the *umātapharaha*.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: नः समाधिमावयदि क्लेशांश्चप्रतन्मकरोति प्रतन्मकृतक्लेशांन् प्रसंख्यानाग्निनादग्धबीजकस्यानप्रसवधर्मिणः करिष्यति ते षांतनूकरणायपुनः क्लेशैरखरासृष्ट्सत्पुरुषान्यमतामात्रख्या तिः सूक्ष्मप्रज्ञासमाप्ताधिकांराः प्रतिप्रसवयकरिष्यंति तेषां तनूकरणात्पुनः क्लेशैः अयपुनः क्लेशः वे कियंतेवेति अधिद्या सेत्रमुतरेषांप्रसुव्तनुविच्छिन्दोदाराणां ४ अत्रअविद्यासे त्रप्रसवभूमिरुत्तरेषां अस्मितादीनां चतुविकाल्पानांप्रसुव्त नुविच्छिन्दोदाराणां तत्रकामसुप्तिः चेतसिन्नक्तिमात्रप्रतिष्ठा नाबीजभावोपगमः ता प्रबोधओलेबनेसंमुखीभावः
Final_Translation: That which brings about our meditative absorption (samadhi), attenuates afflictions (kleshas), and—once the seeds of those afflictions have been burned away by the fire of discriminative discernment (prasamkhyana)—renders them incapable of future germination: for the sake of further thinning those [remaining subtle afflictions], the mere realization of the distinction between the true Self and the transformative constituents of nature, which has exhausted its domain, will bring about their dissolution (pratiprasava). Because of this attenuation, how can those afflictions arise again? Here, the text answers: Regarding [avidya] being the field for the subsequent ones—which exist in dormant, attenuated, severed, or fully active states—avidya is the soil and source of the subsequent [afflictions such as egoism and the rest], existing in these four states: dormant, attenuated, interrupted, or active. Therein, deep sleep (kamasupti) is the rest of the mind, established merely in consciousness, attaining a state of seed-like potentiality; awakening is the arising into manifest presence upon the acquisition of support.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: राम॰ १ ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः अथद्वितीयः पादः उद्दिष्टः समाहितचित्तस्य योगः कथंमुत्थितचित्तोपियोगयुक्तः स्यादित्येतदुद्दारभ्यते तपस्वा ध्यायेश्वरप्रणिधाना निक्रियायोगः १ नार्तापसिनोयोगः सिध्यति अनादिश्शंकर्मवासनाचित्राप्रकृष्तष्ठापितविषयजाला चांसुद्धि र्नांतरेणतपः संभेदमापद्यते रुतितपसमुपादनानेन च चितप्रसा दनमबाधमानमनेनासेव्य मितिमन्यंतेस्वाध्यायः प्रणवादिप वित्रमंत्राणांजपः मोक्षशास्त्र्रध्यायनंवा ईश्वरप्रणिधानेसर्व क्रियाणांपरमगुरौवर्णं तत्फलसंस्यासोवा सहिक्रियायोगः समाधिभावनायः क्लेशतनूकरणार्थश्र २ सहिज्ञासेव्यमा शिक १
Final_Translation: Om. Salutations to Lord Ganesha. Now the second pada is introduced.   Having explained the yoga of one whose mind is collected, it is now begun to explain how yoga is attainable even for one whose mind is distracted.   Austerity (tapas), study of sacred texts (svadhyaya), and devotion to the Lord (ishvara-pranidhana) constitute Kriya Yoga. Yoga does not succeed for one who lacks austerity. Because the beginningless mind, variegated by karmic impressions and firmly established in a net of sense objects, cannot undergo purification without the shattering force of austerity, austerity must be practiced.   And through the application of austerity, the pacification of the mind is achieved without obstruction; therefore, it is considered worthy of being practiced.   Study (svadhyaya) is the repetition of sacred mantras beginning with Om, or the study of scriptures concerning liberation.   Devotion to the Lord (ishvara-pranidhana) is the dedication of all actions to the supreme Guru, or the renunciation of the fruits of those actions.   This very Kriya Yoga is for the purpose of bringing about meditative absorption (samadhi-bhavana) and for diminishing the afflictions (klesha-tanukarana-artham). This alone should be practiced...

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: यदादमत्यशब्दोविकारार्थमदैपधावाथ्र्संपच्छनइत्याह योगानुशासनांशस्त्रमधिकृतमिति ननुडद्यायानुमाननया योगोऽधिकृतो मनुशास्त्रमित्यत आह वेदितब्यमिति मुक्तं श्रुत्वाध्यमाननया योग इत्युक्तं मनुतदिमयेराशास्त्रेणकारणोन बुताथा वर सांगोभरखयुता दकस्यव्यापारोन कर्मगोचर इतिकर्तृव्यापारविवक्षया योगविषयत्थशास्त्रस्याधिकृतत्वात्चेदितव्यं शास्त्रव्यापारगोचरतयानुयोगएवा धिकृत इतिभाव । अधिकारार्थस्यचाथ्र्यद्वयस्याथ्र्यनीयमानोदकुनदकीन निबंधग्रंथोगलाळ यिनिल्यम् । जिमेन के शब्दसंदेहनि मित्तमर्थसंदेहोनुपब्यति । योगःसमाधिः युञ्जसमाधावितिसत्ता छुत्यन्तर समाधथ्र्षे नतु युजिर्र्मोगे इयस्मार्थंसंयोगाथ्र्इत्यर्थः । ननु योगातुशासनंेशास्त्रमधिकृतं वेदितव्यम् । योगःसमाधिः । नचमार्थ मोमः । चित्तस्यधर्मः ॥ १ ॥
Final_Translation: When the non-mortal word indicates the meaning of transformation and is pursued for the sake of wealth, one asks: "Is this the authoritative treatise on the discipline of yoga?" Since yoga is established through inferential reasoning, and the treatise is that of Manu, he says: "It is to be known." Having heard this directly as the path of study, it is said that yoga is [taught] by Manu through this authoritative text; therefore, it is not grasped by the unlearned through mere literal sense.   Because the operation of the supreme reality does not fall within the domain of ritual action, and because the scriptural text concerning yoga is authoritative by virtue of intending the operation of the agent, the underlying intent is that inquiry alone is authorized as falling within the domain of scriptural operation. And for the dual purpose of authority, the text composed by Udaka and Nadakina remains constantly profound to be grasped. Where there is no doubt regarding words, no doubt regarding meaning arises.   Yoga is *samādhi* (absorption), derived from the verbal root *yuj samādhau* denoting existence, as confirmed by other scriptural passages indicating the meaning of *samādhi*, and not from the root *yujir yoge* which has the meaning of conjunction.   Now, one asks: "Is the authoritative treatise understood to be 'the discipline of yoga'?" Yoga is *samādhi*. And *samādhi* is not liberation; rather, it is a quality of the mind.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: न तु नाड्याश्च वक्त्रावकालो भेषजयोऽङ्गकृत् शोधने शम ने चेति समासाद्योषधे द्विधा शरीरज्ञानां रोगाणां क्रमेणापरमी क्ष्यथम् । वस्तिर्विरिको वमने तथा तैलचूर्णमधुः घीवैर्यक्तताशि वितानमनुरोघो षधे परम् भिषद्द्वयाद्युप्स्यातारो वीणादा चत्तप्तयं चिकित्तित्सानिर्दिष्टं प्रत्येके चत्रयेणम् दप्तस्त्री यांतृशास्त्रा यो त्सकं माशुविभिषक वडकल्पं प्रहूर्णैणमः स्मात्रयोगममोषधम् श्रव्रक्तसुविदेत्तो मतिमान्न्यारवा रके प्राज्ञो रोगी भिषावशेपात्तापकस्मात्त्वानोपि सर्वोषधत्तमेः रेरेगनः पुंसोजितात्मनः श्रममंगल्पदेतग्रड्इपेषोनुपद् वः मृतलहृधरोघेत्प्रतिपारसेपरि गृहेग्रनुगलेयेकदो चमागोडाभृवतः शस्त्रादिसाधनः क्रूक्षसंकरेखवतनागदः शेषहतायैवायाः पथ्याभ्यासाहिपयंगे अनएक्रसपवः
Final_Translation: However, the orifice of the tubular vessel (nadi) does not render the medicine effective for purification (shodhana) and pacification (shamana). Thus, having attained medicine in two ways, the knowers of the body should subsequently examine it in relation to diseases: enema (vasti), purgation (virecana), emesis (vamana), as well as formulation with oil, powder, honey, and ghee, along with the mitigation of resistance, constitutes supreme medicine. The physicians and instructors, possessing musical instruments, have prescribed a triad of treatments, with each triad consisting of three parts. The disciplined physician, intent upon the surgical science, quickly brings forth the proper formulation, acting as an antidote. The intelligent patient, recognizing this, submits to the authority of the physician, thereby eliminating torment. For a self-controlled person free from disease, exertion brings auspicious results without distress. Overcoming the obstruction of the heart's vessels, one dwells happily at home. Abandoning fierce means such as weapons and poisons, and engaging in wholesome diet and regimen, one attains ultimate well-being.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: ताभ्यां वा मनसः स्थितिं संपादयेत्॥३५॥ विषयवती वा प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना मन सः स्थितिं निबध्नती॥ नासिकाग्रे धारयतो अस्या दिव्यगंधसंविदगंधप्रव ृत्तिः॥ जिह्वाग्रे दिव्यरससंविद् तालुनि रूपसंविद् जिह्वामध्ये दिव्यस्पर्शसं वित्॥ जिह्वामूले दिव्यशब्दसंविद् इत्येताः प्रवृत्तयउत्पन्नाश्चित्तं स्थितौ निबध्नतीति संशयं विधमन्ति· समाधिप्रज्ञायाश्च द्वारी भवन्तीति· एतेन च न्द्रादियग्रह मणिप्रदीप रस्मादिषु प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना विषयवत्येव वेदितव्या॥ यद्यपित्र शास्त्रानुमानाचार्य्योपदेशैरवगतमर्थन तं प्रज्ञोतमेव भवति एतेषां यथार्त्यतार्थप्रतिपादनसामर्थ्यं तथापियावदेकदेशोपिकारिणा स्वकरणासंवेद्यो भवति तावत्सवै परोक्षमिव अपवर्गादिषु सूक्ष्मेष्वर्थेषु न दृढां बुद्धिमुपादयति। तस्माच्छास्त्रानुमानाचार्य्योपदेशयोर्द्धलनाथे
Final_Translation: By those means also, one should accomplish the stability of the mind. Or, a sense-perceiving activity, when arisen, firmly establishes the stability of the mind. When one concentrates upon the tip of the nose, there arises the experience and activity of divine fragrance. At the tip of the tongue, there is the experience of divine taste; on the palate, the experience of form; in the middle of the tongue, the experience of divine touch; and at the root of the tongue, the experience of divine sound. These very activities, when arisen and binding the mind in stability, dispel doubts and become the gateways to the knowledge of concentration (samādhi). By this same principle, it is to be understood that activities arising in connection with the moon, sun, planets, gems, lamps, and rays are likewise sense-perceiving in nature. Even though an object understood through scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher does not become fully realized wisdom possessing the direct capacity to reveal truth as it actually is—yet, as long as even a single aspect of it is not directly experienced by one's own faculties, it remains, as it were, indirect, and does not produce a firm conviction regarding subtle matters such as liberation and the like. Therefore, for the sake of strengthening [the understanding derived from] scripture, inference, and the instruction of a teacher, [direct experience is necessary].

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: पातं. १३ मेवावश्यं कश्चिदर्थविशेषः प्रपक्षीकर्तव्यः । तत्र तदुपदिष्टार्थेकदेशप्रपक्षते सति सर्वं सुसक्ष्मविषयमति आपवर्गीनुप्रदीयते । एतदर्थमेवेदं चित्तपरिकर्म निर्दिश्यते । अनियतासु वृत्तिषु तद्विषयायां वशीकारसंज्ञायामुपजातायां समर्थः स्यात् तस्य तस्यर्थस्य प्रपक्षीकरणाय तथा च सति श्रद्धावीर्यस्मृतिसमाधयोऽस्याप्रतिबंधेन भविषयंतीति ॥ ३५॥। विशोका वा ज्योतिष्मती पुरुषस्य ॥ प्रवृत्तिरूत्पन्ना मनसः स्थितिinibandhनी सन्युच्यते हृदयपुंडरीके धारयतो या बुद्धि संवित् ॥ बुद्धिसं हि भास्वरमाकाशकल्प्यम् ॥ तत्र स्थिति वैशारद्यात्तः प्रक्रतिः सूर्येदुग्रहमणिप्रभारूपाकारेण विकल्प्पते । तथा चास्मितायां समापन्ने चित्ते निस्तैरगमहोधधिकल्प्यं शांतं मनंतमस्मितामात्रं भवति । यत्रेदममुक्तं तन्मात्रमात्रमात्मान मनुविद्यास्मीति राम १३
Final_Translation: Certainty indeed requires that a particular object be singled out as the primary focus. When a specific part of the teaching is thus made the primary focus, the intellect, possessing an extremely subtle range of perception, is directed toward liberation. It is precisely for this purpose that this mental purification is prescribed. When the fluctuating mental modifications are unstable, and the state of mastery over those objects arises, one becomes capable of making this or that object the primary focus. When this is the case, faith, energy, mindfulness, and deep concentration will arise unobstructed for him.   Or, [concentration may be attained] by [meditating on] the sorrowless and luminous [state] of the Purusha. The arising of [divine] activity is said to be the stabilizing support of the mind, when one concentrates the intellect's awareness upon the lotus of the heart. For the intellect is indeed radiant and resembles the ether. There, through proficiency in stability, that [intellect] manifests in the forms of the brilliance of the sun, moon, planets, and gems. And thus, when the mind is absorbed in the sense of 'I-am-ness' (asmita), the mind becomes tranquil, infinite, like an ocean devoid of waves, consisting solely of 'I-am-ness.' Concerning this, it has been said: "Knowing the Self as merely that, one becomes 'I am'."

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्। नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ १६ ॥
Final_Translation: I see You with many arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes, everywhere of infinite form. I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor yet Your beginning, O Lord of the Universe, O Universal Form.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: न। तणादिका व्यख्यावकालो भेषजयोऽगकृत् शोधने शम ने चेशि समासायोषधे द्विधा शरीरज्ञाना रोघाण क्रमेणपरमो त्तमम्। वान्तिरिवरेको वमने तथा तै लञ्चुते नमधुः पीवैर्याक्ताशि तंतान मनोरोधो षधे परम् भिषद्ख्या एषण्याता रोगी पादा वत्तस्ये चिकित्सितानि रिहृये प्रत्ते के चञ्चत्रगुणाम् दतस्तो यात्तृषास्त्रायो तत्सकमाशुविभिषक वडकल्पञ्चाहूयणेसं मन्त्रो गयप्रमोघथम् अत्र रक्तसुविदेत्तो मतिमान् यारवारकैः आज्ञो रोगीभिषब्वेशेपात कपस्मारत्वनापे सर्वोषधत्तमे रैदेषनः पुंसो जितात्मनः श्रमनम्गोल्यदेतत्रइउपहुनोपद वः श्रुतलव्हरोघन्त प्रतिपार से परि गृहे यत्रु यले शेकदो धमागोडाऽमृतवः शस्त्रादिसाधनः क्रुद्धस करे च्चनतो गदः शेषहता रागयायाळः पथ्याभ्यासाहिपयंगे अत्र पक्रसपवः
Final_Translation: Not at all. The time for the explanation of grasses and other materials is not [appropriate here]. The physician, acting effectively in both purification (shodhana) and pacification (shamana), [should understand] that medicines are twofold. For the knowledge of the body, obstructions are sequentially the highest and best. Just as emesis (vamana) and purgation (virechana), so too in emesis, [along] with oils, salt, and honey, drunk and combined with food, it is supreme as a treatment for mental blockages.   The physician, [well-]versed in probing, having approached the patient, [should examine] his feet and vital parts. Treatments given to the heart... [and regarding] the qualities of the water... thirst and distress... immediately the physician, calling upon the five kalpas, with the incantation to dispel diseases... Here, the wise man, having well-known blood through the use of... command the patient and the physician... epilepsy, skin diseases, and the best of all medicines...   The fatigue of a man of disciplined self is overcome... here the affliction... the destruction of sacred knowledge... protection in the household where... weapons and other means... the angry disease... the eradication of passion... the practice of wholesome diet and lifestyle... Here is the final settling.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसंघान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
Final_Translation: O God, within your body I see all the gods, as well as the diverse hosts of beings—Lord Brahma seated on the lotus throne, all the rishis, and the celestial serpents.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: ॥श्रीरामाय नमः॥ उंका ऋषभं ममरू्लै निरा कारव्यापतते सच रातस्मैश्रीगुरवेन म परमगुरवेनम॥
Final_Translation: Salutation to Sri Rama. Obeisances to the Supreme Guru, the auspicious bull [among gurus], who is formless and all-pervading, and who illuminates the moving and the unmoving. Obeisances to the supreme guru.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा। अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा॥ १३॥
Final_Translation: There, at that time, the son of Pandu beheld the entire universe, divided in manifold ways, standing as one in the body of the God of gods.
